ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the left side is an aromatic six-membered ring, with R connected below the ring and N connected to the right side of the ring. N is also connected respectively to O on the right and O below; the right-side O is connected upward to a carbon chain, and the top of this carbon chain shows a C=C double bond. The lower O is connected to Mg, and Mg is connected to Br. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem asks to ignore the arrows. Then reason: Count by components according to the specified method. Around the aromatic ring there are 6 C-C connections. Non-ring connections include: 1 ring-R, 1 ring-N, 1 N-O (right side), 1 N-O (lower), 1 lower O-Mg, 1 Mg-Br, 1 right-side O-C vertical connection, and 1 C=C alkene connection, for a total of 8. Total = 6 + 8 = 14.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. method.method_draft: Count bonds by components. First count the six C-C connections around the aromatic ring. Then count all non-ring connections shown: ring-R, ring-N, N-O to the right, N-O downward, lower O-Mg, Mg-Br, right O-C vertical, and the C=C alkene connection. Add these component counts, excluding any implicit hydrogens and ignoring arrows, to obtain the total.
